newsitem.title: FRANCE: Models bare it all as nudity makes a comeback.
newsitem.headline: Models bare it all as nudity makes a comeback.

text.p: - Nakedness is making a comeback on the Paris catwalk, where designers set on maximum exposure are peeling off the layers and betting on a steamy summer.
After the topless torsos in shows by Christian Dior and Dice Kayek this week, German designer Karl Lagerfeld focused on lingerie in his ready-to-wear collection for the house of Chloe.
Apparently convinced that undress was the best form of dress, he gave more than a peek at bouncing breasts beneath sheer babydolls and buttocks under hiked-up silk panties with matching bras.
There was a taste of everything -- soft separates of day-glo floral prints on black, lace-edged stretch knee-pants, sheer pink chiffon camisoles and teddies.
Afro-coiffed models on neck-breaking six-inch (15-cm) heels sported splashy satin bellbottoms with halter tops and skinny jackets, lace-up suede ensembles and psychedelic LSD prints.
For evening, Lagerfeld flecked pale chiffon gowns with feathers or sequins, and sketched fluorescent cala lilies on black.

"He gave us a lot to choose from. We can do the 70s, we can do a little of the 30s and a little of the 60s," said Joan Kaner, vice-president of fashion direction for Neiman Marcus department stores. "The prints were very strong."
Chloe officials would not confirm media reports that Lagerfeld has decided to leave the house when his contract expires in March 1997.
If he does leave, Chloe will join the long list of Paris houses, including Givenchy, Christian Dior and Guy Laroche, that have had to seek new designers.
At Nina Ricci, Miriam Schaeffer revived the riding coats, starch collars and neckties of her equestrian dandy look, this time pairing them with vinyl shorts barely covering models' bottoms.
These, hopefully, were theatrical props meant only for the catwalk, for who could possibly imagine Nina Ricci's mature, demure clientele showing so much at afternoon tea?

Beside the knickers -- and variations on Schaeffer's jacket in pastel brocades with matching go-go boots and an S & M evening version with bondage platform heels -- not much was on offer unless flashy sequined minis under bright terrycloth coats with swansdown ruffs are wearable anywhere else than to a drag club.
Angelo Tarlazzi kept things simple -- slim and slinky knits, with cardigans brushing the floor over bellbottoms, and midriffs bared between tube tops and low-slung minis.
Tarlazzi kept the silhouette streamlined, trotting out grey wool novice dresses over crisp white tailored shirts and pinstriped trouser ensembles and jumpsuits with necklines low on the shoulder.
For evening he showed lavender bias-cut gowns of silk and satin or brushstroked colour on white chiffon.
The fashion season, featuring nearly 90 scheduled shows and another 40 by appointment, runs through next week when Givenchy and Christian Dior are set to announce the appointment of new designers.
